claims.text: AlCoCrFeNi-based high-entropy alloys exhibit inherently sluggish diffusion.
A controlled Al or Cr concentration gradient governs selective outward migration of the reactive element.
Selective outward migration of Al or Cr forms an ultrathin, stable Al2O3 or Cr2O3 surface layer.
The Al2O3 or Cr2O3 layer provides long-term oxidation resistance at high temperature.
Systematically changing Al or Cr content adjusts diffusion kinetics without significantly altering the alloy's overall configurational entropy.
High configurational entropy induces inherently sluggish diffusion in the HEA.
Sluggish diffusion combined with an engineered reactive-element concentration gradient promotes controlled selective oxidation.
Controlled selective oxidation produces a thin, adherent protective oxide scale.
The thin, adherent oxide scale limits further oxidation.
Lower-entropy alloys have less controlled diffusion, leading to rapid oxide thickening or spallation.
Relative to a lower-entropy single-phase baseline, an HEA with optimized Al or Cr content will form a more uniform, ultrathin, and stable protective oxide and exhibit a lower oxidation rate.
The proposed mechanism is expected to dominate during isothermal oxidation in air at 1000–1200 °C.
Insufficient reactive-element concentration fails to form the protective oxide.
Excessive reactive-element concentration leads to uncontrolled oxide growth.
Existing diffusion studies in HEAs support the concept of sluggish diffusion.

contradictions.description: The initial alloy is specified as uniform and the intervention varies bulk Al or Cr content, but the central mechanism requires a controlled or engineered concentration gradient. The experiment does not state how such a gradient is introduced or measured.

The optimized alloy is predicted to outperform the baseline, but the falsification rule treats sudden degradation after a minor composition change as falsifying the hypothesis even though the hypothesis also posits a bounded composition window; crossing that window could therefore be consistent with, rather than contradictory to, the hypothesis.
